query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a small amount of a grain-boundary–strengthening element (specifically Nb at approximately 0.5–1 at%) during alloy synthesis of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 will improve its load-bearing integrity without degrading its caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high‐entropy alloy as presently synthesized, which exhibits a large caloric response but poor mechanical integrity with a tendency to form cracks.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled 0.5–1 at% Nb during the alloying process to achieve Nb segregation to grain boundaries and promote fine-scale precipitation that reinforces the microstructure.
generation.conditions: Samples are processed under otherwise identical melting and casting conditions with the only change being the Nb addition. Testing is performed under the same applied magnetic field, pressure field, temperature regime, and mechanical loading conditions as the baseline, ensuring the operational boundaries remain unchanged.
generation.structural_mediator: Nb-induced grain boundary segregation and formation of nanoscale precipitates that act to hinder crack initiation and propagation.
generation.mechanism: The Nb additions are expected to strengthen the grain boundaries, reducing intergranular crack formation under mechanical load. With the doping level kept low, the key phase transition features responsible for the large caloric effect (magnetocaloric and barocaloric performance) should remain essentially unaffected.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Nb-doped alloy will show significantly improved load-bearing integrity (e.g., increased fracture toughness and reduced crack density) while retaining a caloric response comparable to the undoped alloy under identical fields.
generation.baseline: The undoped (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, which has high caloric performance but suffers from poor load-bearing characteristics.
generation.boundary: The alloy is evaluated under the same magnetic field, pressure field, temperature, and mechanical loading limits that define its normal operating regime in refrigeration applications.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty concerning the precise impact of the Nb additions on the caloric phase transition kinetics and entropy changes; the optimal Nb concentration must be confirmed to ensure that caloric performance is not adversely affected.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy samples: one set synthesized with 0.5–1 at% Nb and a control set synthesized under identical conditions without Nb. Conduct mechanical testing (e.g., fracture toughness, crack propagation analysis) and caloric performance measurements (e.g., entropy change, temperature response under applied magnetic and pressure fields) under standard operating conditions.
measurements: Fracture toughness and crack density under mechanical loading
Magnetocaloric/Barocaloric response (e.g., entropy change, adiabatic temperature change)
Phase transition behavior (e.g., transition temperature and hysteresis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Nb-doped samples do not display a statistically significant improvement in mechanical integrity (i.e., higher fracture toughness, lower crack density) relative to the control, or if there is a statistically significant reduction in the magnitude of the caloric response, the hypothesis will be falsified.
